**Premise 1:** ((S ∨ P) ↔ (S ↔ P))

Let me evaluate the truth table for the biconditional:

| S | P | S∨P | S↔P | (S∨P)↔(S↔P) |
|---|---|-----|-----|-------------|
| T | T | T   | T   | **T**       |
| T | F | T   | F   | F           |
| F | T | T   | F   | F           |
| F | F | F   | T   | F           |

The biconditional is true **only** when S = T and P = T. Therefore, we can conclude **S ∧ P**.

**Premise 2:** (R ↔ Q)

This is given as a fact, so we carry it through.

**Combined conclusion:**

(S ∧ P) ∧ (R ↔ Q)

<answer>(S ∧ P) ∧ (R ↔ Q)</answer>
